findings.title: Category SQL injection exposes unpublished products
findings.controlled_input: The unauthenticated category query parameter, demonstrated with category=books%27+OR+1%3D1+--+.
findings.broken_boundary: User input is interpolated into SQL, bypassing the category and published filters.
findings.runtime_evidence: An ordinary books request returned only published product 1. The injected request returned products 1, 2 and 3, including unpublished product 2.
findings.remedy: Bind category as a SQL parameter.

findings.title: Signed-in user can read another user's invoice
findings.controlled_input: An authenticated user controls the invoice ID in /api/invoices/{id}.
findings.broken_boundary: Authentication succeeds, but the fetched invoice's owner is never compared with the signed-in user.
findings.runtime_evidence: With alice-test-token, /api/invoices/2 returned Bob's invoice and amount 200.
findings.remedy: Query by both invoice ID and authenticated owner, returning 404 when no matching row exists.

findings.title: Download path traversal exposes internal data
findings.controlled_input: The unauthenticated name query parameter, demonstrated with name=..%2Finternal%2Fnotes.txt.
findings.broken_boundary: The constructed path is read without enforcing that its resolved location remains under data/public.
findings.runtime_evidence: The traversal returned the synthetic content of data/internal/notes.txt; a normal request returned data/public/readme.txt.
findings.remedy: Resolve the requested path and reject any path outside the resolved data/public directory.
